# montecarlo_hive_mysql_credentials (Resource)

Hive (MySQL) credentials are the login Monte Carlo stores for the MySQL database behind a Hive metastore. A Data Lake warehouse's metadata connection uses them. The password is never returned.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `db_name` (String) MySQL database that holds the Hive metastore.
- `host` (String) Hostname of the database endpoint.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of the database user. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `password_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `port` (Number) Port the database listens on.
- `user` (String) Database user Monte Carlo logs in as.

### Optional

- `ssl_ca_url` (String) https URL of the PEM bundle of certificate authorities the MySQL server's certificate is checked against. Monte Carlo downloads it at each connection and connects over TLS. For Amazon RDS, use https://truststore.pki.rds.amazonaws.com/global/global-bundle.pem. Leave it out and the server's certificate is not checked.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
